slides.headline:
You don't need
heavy weights to
build [hl]muscle.[/hl]
slides.sub: 49 trained men. 12 weeks. Light vs heavy.

image.label: real
image.alt: Dan at the top of a dumbbell lateral raise by his pool, smiling

slides.headline: Trained men lifted for 12 weeks. One group went light for 20 to 25 reps. One went heavy for 8 to 12. Every set to failure.
slides.note: The heavy group gained more on bench press: 14 kg vs 9 kg.
slides.source: Morton et al., Journal of Applied Physiology, 2016

slides.title:
Effort counts,
[hl]not the plate.[/hl]

image.label: real
image.alt: Dan holding light dumbbells out at shoulder height

items: Pick a weight you can lift 8 to 25 times.
Stop when you can't do one more clean rep.
Sore joints? Go lighter. You'll keep growing.
Want a bigger bench? Go heavier there.

slides.headline:
Take every set
[y]close to failure.[/y]
The weight is your call.
slides.body: Light or heavy, the men who pushed every set to failure grew the same.

image.label: real
image.alt: Dan now, shirtless, hands behind his head

slides.save: Save this for the next time someone tells you to go heavy or go home.
